name: The Spirit in Sanctification and Assurance
path: Pneumatology: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit

objectives.text: Identify the Holy Spirit as the helper God gives to make his people more like Jesus
Name the nine fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians 5:22-23
Pray a short class prayer asking God for the help of the Holy Spirit, based on Jesus' promise in Luke 11:13
Recall from Romans 8:26 that the Holy Spirit helps God's people when they pray
Describe how each fruit of the Spirit can be shown in everyday actions at home and school
Summarize Paul's contrast between walking by the Spirit and gratifying the desires of the flesh
Explain why Scripture calls these qualities the fruit of the Spirit rather than the product of human effort alone
Define sanctification in the words of the Westminster Shorter Catechism and explain its key phrases
Compare grieving the Spirit and quenching the Spirit using the context of each command
Identify the Word, sacraments, and prayer as the ordinary means the Spirit uses to sanctify believers
Apply Paul's call to keep in step with the Spirit to concrete situations of temptation and choice
Distinguish justification from sanctification as the Reformed tradition confesses them
Analyze Romans 8:15-16 to explain the Spirit's witness with the believer's spirit that believers are children of God
Explain mortification and vivification as the Spirit's work in which believers actively put sin to death and live to righteousness
Interpret the Spirit's intercession with groanings in Romans 8:26-27 within the context of Romans 8:18-30
Explain how Scripture's language of the Spirit as seal and guarantee relates to the believer's security
Explain the three grounds of assurance named in the Westminster Confession and the Scripture behind each
Explain why the Reformed tradition teaches that assurance is attained through ordinary means without extraordinary revelation
Explain the command to be filled with the Spirit within its context of worship and household relationships
Analyze Romans 7:14-25 alongside the Westminster Confession to describe the ongoing conflict between the Spirit and remaining corruption
Explain the Reformed teaching that a believer's assurance may be shaken and later renewed by the Spirit
Construct a summary theology of the Spirit's role in progressive sanctification drawing on key texts and confessional statements
Evaluate perfectionist claims about the Spirit-filled life in light of Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Evaluate the relationship between the Spirit's witness and the Word as grounds of assurance against claims that rest assurance on private revelation or feeling alone
Compare the Reformed confession that believers may be assured of salvation with the Council of Trent's teaching on assurance
Write an essay synthesizing how the Spirit as seal, firstfruits, and guarantee links present sanctification to final redemption

changes: Merged the kindergarten helper objective with the grade 3 'more like Jesus' observation. Kept and reworded the fruit, prayer, flesh and Spirit, grieving and quenching, keep in step, inward witness, groanings, sealing, ordinary means of assurance, progressive sanctification, perfectionism, Spirit and Word, and seal and guarantee objectives. Verse ranges were widened to include context. Added a class prayer practice and the everyday expression of the fruit. Added objectives on the catechism definition of sanctification, the means of grace, the justification and sanctification distinction, and mortification and vivification. Also added being filled with the Spirit, the three grounds of assurance in WCF 18.2, remaining corruption in WCF 13.2-3, shaken and renewed assurance in WCF 18.4, and a Reformed versus Trent comparison. Regeneration and indwelling are left to the sibling sub-topic. Confession citations now use full document names.
